claim: The author's one interpretation is sound, and it is necessary: a subcheck is keyed only when the baseline holds its rows in full. Without it, a subcheck keyed now but held as a sample by the baseline would still count as partial on the baseline side, so neither its buckets nor its total would be judged. An off-branch rise inside an existing non-staleness bucket would then pass. Pre-existing rows on a touched file past the baseline's cap would block. Both contradict the kind rules the brief says apply: pre-existing or improved counts never block, and a grown bucket that is not staleness stops the landing. test_a_baseline_that_holds_only_a_sample_is_not_compared_with_an_export protects the condition.

file: scripts/pm-landing-check.py (key_from_exports, replace_rows); reports/landing-checks/README.md ('What this leaves open')
claim: A keyed subcheck is judged only on its export's rows, and the aggregate's printed rows are discarded. The export is a second run, matched to the aggregate by total alone. So when a row the aggregate printed is absent from the export at an equal total, that row is never judged, even a failure on a touched file that is not staleness. The base script judged every printed row. It is a false pass, the unsafe direction. It needs a second run that differs from the first at the same count. That happens when the shared checkout's working tree changes between the runs (other threads' uncommitted work, which AGENTS.md already names as a hazard) or the validator code changes. Validator nondeterminism is not a route: the real validators I ran twice gave identical rows. The README states the limit ('the rows are not compared one by one'). But its sentence 'The equal total is the evidence that it saw what the aggregate saw' claims more than a total shows, and the L-07 pairing in the same script does not accept a total alone as that evidence.
evidence: E3 (cases/scenarios.py). The aggregate prints 133 rows, row 5 of which is {'path': 'Plans/storage-plan.md', 'error': 'missing_ref', 'ref': '#gone'} on a touched file. The export holds the fixture's 133 rows. Tip: exit 1, '[keyed    ] run-gates/validate_plan_graph (50 of 133 printed): its export (validate-plan-graph) holds all 133 rows, the printed total: 132 staleness, 1 pre-existing', and the missing_ref appears nowhere. Base: exit 2, with '[blocking    ] run-gates/validate_plan_graph  missing_ref  Plans/storage-plan.md  {"ref":"#gone"}' and the same for audit-governance (cases/e2e-out/E3-row-swap-equal-total.txt). pair_validators already requires 'every row the run-gates copy printed is among its rows' as the evidence that two runs saw the same inputs. On the real validators the guard would not fall back without cause. In a full checkout of the tip in my clone, the record run's export of validate-prd-planning-runtime-contracts held 1240 rows, the printed total, and both aggregates' printed rows were exactly its first 50 and 100 rows in order (logs/real_printed_vs_export_record.txt). validate-plan-graph, validate-evidence, validate-prd-planning-runtime-contracts, lint-path-refs, json-syntax and validate-implementation-readiness each gave the same rows in the same order under PYTHONHASHSEED 1 and 2 (logs/real_determinism.txt). So a second run differs from the first only when the tree or the validator code changes between them. tree_state is taken after the second aggregate, not after the exports, so no version check covers the export runs.
suggested_repair: This adds a fallback case beyond the brief's list, so it needs the coordinator's go; without it, record an open question. The repair: in key_from_exports, take the printed items and, before a subcheck is keyed, compute missing = Counter(printed keys of (check, subcheck)) - Counter(keys of the export's normalized rows). If missing is not empty, set row['case'] = 'rows_mismatch' and row['reason'] = f"its export ({argv[0]}) holds all {len(failures)} rows, but {n} of the rows the aggregate printed {'is' if n == 1 else 'are'} not among them", so that the truncated rule applies. Add E3 as a test. In the README, add the bullet '*rows mismatch*: the export holds the printed total, but a row the aggregate printed is not among its rows, so it did not see what the aggregate saw', and replace 'The equal total is the evidence that it saw what the aggregate saw; the rows are not compared one by one.' with 'The equal total and every printed row being among its rows are the evidence that it saw what the aggregate saw.'
